## TL;DR

`replaceSection` in `src/core/task.ts` inserted any brand-new `## Heading`
immediately before `## Activity`. On a freeform task the body is raw prompt,
`## Original prompt`, `## Screenshots`, `## Activity` — so the PM agent's
Problem / Desired UX / Acceptance criteria / Notes for AI landed below the
long raw capture and screenshots, and the task panel looked unfleshed-out
(seen on #1030). A new section (anything other than Original prompt,
Screenshots, or Activity) is now inserted before the first of `## Original
prompt` / `## Screenshots` / `## Activity` that exists. Replacing an existing
section stays in place; Original prompt / Screenshots themselves are still
created immediately before Activity, as before. Five new unit tests cover the
ordering; all 36 tests in the `replaceSection` suite pass.

## Work and rationale

The entire fix is the `insertAt` computation in `replaceSection`
(`src/core/task.ts`). Before:

```ts
const activityStart = sectionStart(lines, ACTIVITY_HEADING);
const insertAt = start === -1 ? (activityStart === -1 ? lines.length : activityStart) : start;
```

After, three cases:

1. The heading already exists (`start !== -1`) — replace in place, unchanged.
   This preserves the "replaces an existing section in place without
   reordering later sections" behavior.
2. The new heading IS `## Original prompt` or `## Screenshots` — insert before
   `## Activity`, exactly as today. The task's acceptance criterion 2 ("no
   change to how Original prompt / Screenshots / Activity themselves are
   placed") is what forces this carve-out: without it, re-creating a missing
   Original prompt section would land before Screenshots, which would reorder
   the raw-capture tail.
3. Anything else new — insert before the earliest of `## Original prompt`,
   `## Screenshots`, `## Activity` that exists, else append. Because each
   sequential add lands immediately before the same anchor, Problem, Desired
   UX, Acceptance criteria, Notes for AI keep their insertion order when added
   one at a time (each new section slots in after the previously added ones,
   ahead of the anchor).

The doc comment on `replaceSection` was updated to describe the new placement
so the next reader does not have to reverse-engineer `insertAt`.

The PM prompt in `src/server/freeform.ts` was checked per the task's Notes for
AI and needed no change: `taskConventions` lists the spec sections ending with
Activity (unchanged semantics), and `pmPrompt` tells the agent the raw
explanation "is re-appended for you" — still literally true, because
`finalizeFreeformRun` (`src/server/routes/tasks.ts`) builds the final body via
`withOriginalPromptSection(fields.body, explanation)`, which appends
`## Original prompt` at the end of the PM's structured body. The full-pipeline
order (spec first, raw capture last) already matched the desired end state;
only the incremental `replaceSection` path (used by `repoos update --section`
/ `src/server/write.ts` and `human-step-tags.ts`) was wrong.

Tests: five new cases in the `section helpers` describe block of
`src/ui-app/tests/task-protected-sections.test.ts`, next to the existing
`replaceSection` tests:

- new spec section lands above Original prompt and Screenshots;
- sequential adds of Problem → Desired UX → Acceptance criteria → Notes for AI
  keep order ahead of Original prompt / Screenshots / Activity;
- re-replacing an existing section stays in place above the raw capture;
- body with only Activity inserts before it (behaves as today);
- Original prompt and Screenshots themselves are still placed before Activity.

## Approaches tried

The obvious alternative — always insert before the first `## ` anchor of any
kind — was rejected because it would change where Original prompt and
Screenshots land when they are (re-)created, violating acceptance criterion 2.
The two-tier rule (protected tail headings keep the old behavior, everything
else jumps the whole tail) is the minimal change that satisfies both criteria.

I also considered whether the fix belonged in the callers
(`src/server/write.ts`, `src/commands/tasks.ts`, `human-step-tags.ts`) rather
than in `replaceSection` itself. It does not: every mutation path funnels
through `replaceSection`, and the task explicitly scopes the change to the
`insertAt` computation, so fixing it once fixes the PM flow, section updates,
and human-step tagging together.

## Challenges and blockers

Two environmental snags, neither a code problem:

- The scoped `repoos check` run timed out at the 10-minute foreground limit
  (likely queued behind a slot holder / pressure guard). It had already
  committed the fix and tests as an engineer self-check WIP checkpoint
  (`2158eb271`) before timing out, which briefly looked like a lost edit when
  `git status` no longer showed `src/core/task.ts` as modified. `git log`
  confirmed the checkpoint; the only remaining working-tree diff was the
  formatter's reflow of the new tests. Re-ran the check in the background.
- `oxfmt --check` flagged the new test block's formatting (line joining); fixed
  with `oxfmt` on the two touched files, no manual edits needed.

## Key learnings

- `replaceSection` is a chokepoint: one `insertAt` computation governs PM
  flesh-out, CLI section updates, and human-step tagging. Scoping the fix
  there (as the task suggested) avoided touching any caller.
- The freeform pipeline has two independent ordering mechanisms — full-body
  promotion via `withOriginalPromptSection` (already correct: spec first, raw
  capture appended last) and incremental section insertion via
  `replaceSection` (was wrong). The bug only showed in the incremental path,
  which is why the PM output itself looked right while the task panel did not.
- A missing file in `git status` after a timed-out check is worth a `git log`
  before assuming an edit was lost: the self-check checkpoint commit may
  already hold it.
